mainTopic: Birds that fell into fire or were injured: color changes in the innards, the crop, and intestines that came out
overview: This amud opens by finishing the previous discussion: a bird's brain membrane is checked with a wheat straw, and רב שיזבי rules that our geese are treated like water birds. Next comes the משנה's case of a bird that fell into fire. Any amount of greening of the innards makes it a טרפה, and a liver that turned green facing the intestines is a טרפה because it shows the intestines were singed. Two stories teach that the color rule is about change: green is bad only in the naturally red organs (gizzard, heart, liver), and naturally green organs that turned red are also a טרפה. Boiling can reveal whether a color change was only smoke or a real burn, but the גמרא rejects רב אשי's demand to always boil, since we do not presume a defect. A trampled or slammed bird must be checked. A new משנה then lists injuries that leave a bird kosher, and the גמרא discusses רבי's view on a removed crop (ending in תיקו) and the 'roof' of the crop, which is treated like the ושט. Finally, intestines that came out are kosher only if not put back in the wrong order, based on 'הוא עשך ויכוננך', and a story about a man whose intestines came out begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Checking the membrane with a wheat straw
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of the previous discussion: the brain membrane is checked for a hole by using a wheat straw.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a wheat straw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion about how to check whether a bird's brain membrane has a hole. The answer is to use a wheat straw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny hole in the membrane is hard to see. The straw is dragged gently over the membrane, and if it catches somewhere, there is a hole. This answers a practical 'how do we check' question that started before this section.

keyTerms.meaning: With a wheat straw, used as a gentle checking tool

phrases.english: With a wheat straw.
phrases.notes: This finishes an earlier question about checking the brain membrane. If the straw catches, there's a hole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a practical question from before this section about how to examine the brain membrane.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How do we check whether the brain membrane has been pierced?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Drag a wheat straw over it and see whether it catches.

steps.title: Our geese count as water birds
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי rules that the local geese have the same status as water birds for the laws of a crushed skull.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said: These geese of ours are considered like water birds.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי gives a ruling. Geese in his area are treated like water birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא said that a water bird whose skull is crushed is a טרפה even if the membrane is not pierced. רב שיזבי applies that stricter rule to geese, so checking the membrane with a straw does not help for a goose.

keyTerms.meaning: They are similar to, they are treated like

steps.whyThisMatters: It moves geese into the stricter category, so a goose with a crushed skull is a טרפה without any checking.

phrases.english: Rav Sheizvi said:
These geese of ours
are considered like water birds.
phrases.notes: So if a goose's skull is crushed, it is a טרפה even if the membrane is not pierced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule about which birds get the stricter crushed-skull law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Geese are treated like water birds, so a crushed skull alone makes them a טרפה.

steps.title: Any amount of greening is like any size hole
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case of a bird that fell into fire, רבי יוחנן quotes רבי יוסי בן יהושע: any amount of greening of the innards makes the bird a טרפה, just as any size hole does.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if a bird fell into the fire. רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יוסי בן יהושע: The measure for their turning green is like the measure for their being pierced. Just as a hole of any size counts, so too greening of any size counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a bird that fell into fire. Then רבי יוחנן gives the size rule for how much greening of the innards makes the bird a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that singed innards that turned green make the bird a טרפה, but it does not say how much green is needed. רבי יוחנן compares greening to a hole in the innards. Even the smallest hole makes the bird a טרפה, so even the smallest green spot does too.

keyTerms.meaning: It fell into the fire (the משנה's case)
Their being pierced, having a hole
In any amount at all, even the tiniest

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a strict standard: there is no minimum size, so even a small green spot on singed innards makes the bird a טרפה.

phrases.english: If it fell into the fire,
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: a bird fell into fire, and if its innards turned green, it is a טרפה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Yehoshua:
the measure for their turning green is like the measure for their being pierced;
just as their being pierced counts in any amount,
so too their turning green counts in any amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְלָה לָאוּר, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the משנה's case of a bird that fell into fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Greening of the innards in any amount makes the bird a טרפה, just like a hole of any size.

steps.title: A liver that turned green facing the intestines
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks his father, רבי יהושע בן לוי, about a liver that turned green on the side facing the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף, son of רבי יהושע בן לוי, asked רבי יהושע בן לוי: If a liver turned green on the side facing the intestines, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A son asks his father a new question about a green liver. This sets up the ruling that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the discussion was about the innards themselves turning green. Now the question is about the liver turning green, but only on the side that faces the intestines. Is that a problem for the bird?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: Rav Yosef, son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, asked
of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
If a liver turned green on the side facing the intestines,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מֵרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the topic of greening from the innards to the liver.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does greening of the liver on the side facing the intestines make the bird a טרפה?

steps.title: The bird is a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers that the bird is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The father answers his son: such a bird is a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gives a short ruling without a reason. That leaves room for the challenge that follows, which asks why a partly green liver should be worse than a liver that was mostly removed.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten

phrases.english: He said to him: It is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 4.

steps.title: It should be no worse than a removed liver
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges the ruling: a removed liver leaves the bird kosher if some of it remains, so a partly green liver should be no worse.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it be no worse than a liver that was removed!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on the ruling. He compares this case to a liver that was removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When most of a liver is removed but some of it remains, the bird is still kosher. A liver that is only green on one side still has healthy liver left. So why should this bird be a טרפה?

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be no worse than, a comparison to a known case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the removed-liver case makes every bird with a missing liver kosher. It is kosher only when some of the liver remains.

phrases.english: But let it be no worse than where the liver was removed!
phrases.notes: This points to the case where the liver is removed but some of it remains. There the bird is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a liver green on the side facing the intestines makes the bird a טרפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A removed liver does not make the bird a טרפה if some of it remains, so a damaged liver with healthy parts left should not be worse.

steps.title: The green liver shows the intestines were singed
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that a liver green on the side facing the intestines proves the bird fell into fire and its intestines were singed. That is why it is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since the liver turned green on the side facing the intestines, it is clear that the bird fell into the fire and the intestines were singed, and so it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. The problem is not the liver itself but what the green liver tells us about the intestines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Greening on the side that faces the intestines is a sign that fire reached that area. So the intestines themselves were singed, and singed intestines make the bird a טרפה, as the משנה taught. The removed-liver comparison does not apply, because the liver is not the reason for the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: It is known, it is clear

steps.whatToRemember: A liver that turned green facing the intestines makes the bird a טרפה, not because of the liver, but because it proves the intestines were singed by fire.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a sign on one organ can prove damage to another organ, and that damage is what decides the law.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוֹרִיקָה כָּבֵד כְּנֶגֶד בְּנֵי מֵעַיִים –
phrases.english: Since the liver turned green on the side facing the intestines,
it is clear that it fell into the fire,
and the intestines were singed,
and so it is a tereifa.
phrases.notes: It is a טרפה because of the singed intestines, not because of the liver.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוֹרִיקָה כָּבֵד כְּנֶגֶד בְּנֵי מֵעַיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the reason: the ruling is based on the singed intestines, not on the liver.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bird is a טרפה because its liver is damaged, so the removed-liver case should make it kosher.
steps.terutzMaskana: The green liver is a sign that the intestines were singed, and singed intestines make the bird a טרפה.

steps.title: A green-innards hen is ruled kosher
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי sent a hen with green innards to רבי אלעזר הקפר, who declared it kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי had a hen that fell into a fire. He sent it to רבי אלעזר הקפר and told him the innards were green, and רבי אלעזר הקפר ruled it kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real hen with green innards that was ruled kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This seems surprising, because the משנה said green innards are פסול. The story sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A title of honor for a distinguished scholar

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי הַוְיָא לֵיהּ הָהִיא תַּרְנְגוֹלְתָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi had a certain hen,

phrases.aramaic: שַׁדְּרֵיהּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר בְּרִיבִּי,
phrases.english: he sent it before the distinguished Rabbi Elazar HaKappar,
he said to him: they were green,
and he declared it kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי הַוְיָא לֵיהּ הָהִיא תַּרְנְגוֹלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the liver discussion to a practical story about green innards.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hen whose innards turned green after a fire was ruled kosher.

steps.title: But the משנה says green is unfit
steps.stepSummary: The ruling seems to contradict the משנה, which says green innards are פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה that green innards are unfit!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי challenges the kosher ruling by quoting the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to say that green innards always make the bird פסול. So how could this green hen be kosher?

keyTerms.meaning: But surely... (opens a challenge from a known source)

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: "Green ones are unfit"!

steps.kashyaTarget: The kosher ruling on the green hen
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says green innards are unfit, with no exceptions mentioned.

steps.title: Green is unfit only in the gizzard, heart and liver
steps.stepSummary: The rule that green is פסול applies only to the gizzard, heart and liver.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only said green is unfit for the gizzard, the heart and the liver.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר הקפר answers that the משנה's rule about green covers only three organs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three organs are naturally red, so turning green shows that fire damaged them. Other innards, like the intestines, are naturally green, so a green color there means nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: They only said it about... (limits a rule)

steps.confusionAlert: Green is not always bad. It is a problem only in an organ that is supposed to be red.

phrases.english: They did not say "green ones are unfit"
except for the gizzard, the heart and the liver.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Green innards of any kind are unfit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only green in the gizzard, heart or liver is unfit.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms that the green rule applies to the gizzard, heart and liver.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: which innards did they mean? The gizzard, the heart and the liver.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי אלעזר הקפר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly lists the same three organs. This shows that the answer in the last step is the accepted reading of the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (introduces a supporting ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: Green makes a bird a טרפה only in the naturally red organs: the gizzard, heart and liver.

phrases.english: It is also taught so:
About which innards did they say it?
About the gizzard, the heart and the liver.

steps.raayaObject: The answer that green is unfit only in three organs
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the gizzard, heart and liver

steps.title: A red-innards hen is ruled a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר יוסף sent a hen with red innards to רבי אבהו, who ruled it a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר יוסף had a hen that fell into a fire. He sent it to רבי אבהו and told him the innards were red, and רבי אבהו ruled it a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story, this time about red innards that were ruled a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the first story. The משנה said red is kosher, yet this red hen was ruled a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird or animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten
He sent it before him (for a ruling)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהִוא תַּרְנְגוֹלְתָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef had a certain hen,
he sent it before Rabbi Abbahu,
and he said to him: they were red,
and he ruled it a tereifa.
phrases.notes: The one who ruled it a טרפה is רבי אבהו.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהִוא תַּרְנְגוֹלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story with the opposite color and the opposite result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hen whose innards were red after a fire was ruled a טרפה.

steps.title: But the משנה says red is kosher
steps.stepSummary: The ruling seems to contradict the משנה, which says red innards are kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה that red innards are kosher!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר יוסף challenges the טרפה ruling by quoting the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to say that red is always fine. So why should this red hen be a טרפה?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: "Red ones are kosher"!

steps.kashyaTarget: The טרפה ruling on the red hen
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says red innards are kosher.

steps.title: Any change from an organ's natural color is a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: Red that turned green, or green that turned red, is a טרפה. Red is kosher only in the heart, gizzard and liver.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: red that turned green, and green that turned red, make it a טרפה. They only said red is kosher for the heart, the gizzard and the liver.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו explains that the משנה's kosher red refers only to organs that are naturally red.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real test is whether the organ changed from its natural color. Organs that are naturally green, like the intestines, become a טרפה if they turn red, because that change shows fire damage.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule is about change. An organ that loses its natural color through fire makes the bird a טרפה, whichever way the color goes.

phrases.english: He said to him: red ones that turned green
and green ones that turned red are a tereifa;
they did not say "red ones are kosher"
except for the heart, the gizzard and the liver.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Red innards of any kind are kosher.
steps.terutzMaskana: Red is kosher only in naturally red organs. Any color change makes the bird a טרפה.

steps.title: Green that turns red again after boiling is kosher
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני: if red organs turned green but became red again after boiling, the bird is kosher, because the green came only from smoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר חייא said in the name of רבי מני: if red organs turned green, and one boiled them and they became red again, they are kosher. Why? Smoke got into them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני adds a new rule: boiling can show that a green color was only a smoke stain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the redness comes back, the organ was never really burned. Smoke only colored it for a while, so the bird stays kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: They went back (to their earlier state)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Chiyya said that Rabbi Mani said:
red ones that turned green, and one boiled them,
and they turned red again: they are kosher.
What is the reason? Smoke entered them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a test that can overturn the color rule just taught.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Red organs that turned green but turn red again when boiled are kosher. It was only smoke.

steps.title: Red that turns green after boiling is a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק: if red organs stayed red but turned green after boiling, the bird is a טרפה, because boiling revealed the hidden burn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: we too will say that if red organs did not turn green, and one boiled them and they turned green, it is a טרפה. Why? Their shame was revealed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק uses the same boiling test in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Boiling can uncover damage that was hidden at first. If the organs turn green only after boiling, they really were burned, so the bird is a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: We too will say (applying the same logic the other way)
Their shame was revealed, meaning the hidden damage came out

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
We too will say:
red ones that did not turn green, and one boiled them,
and they turned green: it is a tereifa.
What is the reason? Their shame was revealed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי מני's boiling test in the reverse direction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Red organs that turn green only after boiling show a real burn, so the bird is a טרפה.

steps.title: רב אשי: always boil before eating
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי concludes that a bird that fell into fire should be eaten only after its innards are boiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: therefore a person should eat it only boiled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי draws a practical rule from רב נחמן בר יצחק's teaching: always boil first to check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since boiling can expose hidden burns, רב אשי wants every such bird boiled before it is eaten, even when the innards look red and fine. This sets up the rejection in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Therefore,
a person should not eat it except boiled.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird that fell into fire may be eaten only after boiling the innards to check them.

steps.title: We do not assume a defect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's rule, because we do not assume a defect when there is no sign of one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. We do not assume there is a defect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's requirement to always boil first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the innards look normal and red, there is no sign of damage. We do not go looking for a hidden problem, so boiling is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so (rejects the previous statement)
We do not presume a defect exists without evidence

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general principle of הלכה: we do not assume a problem exists without a reason to think so.
steps.whatToRemember: Boiling is a test that can reveal the truth, but it is not required when the innards look normal.

phrases.english: But it is not so,
we do not presume a defect.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב אשי's requirement to boil every bird that fell into fire
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes hidden damage with no evidence, which halacha does not do.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Normal-looking red innards are kosher without boiling.

steps.title: A trampled or slammed bird needs checking
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case of a bird that was trampled or slammed against a wall, רבי אלעזר בן אנטיגנוס rules that all these cases need to be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he trampled it or slammed it against a wall. רבי אלעזר בן אנטיגנוס said in the name of רבי אלעזר בר' ינאי: in both this case and that case, the bird must be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, a trampled or slammed bird, and gives a ruling on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says such a bird is kosher if it lived 24 hours and was then slaughtered. This statement adds that it still must be checked after slaughter to make sure no organ was damaged in a way that makes it a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: He slammed it against a wall
Both this one and that one

phrases.english: He trampled it or slammed it against a wall.
phrases.notes: These words are quoted from the משנה, which goes on to say that such a bird is kosher if it lived 24 hours.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Antigonus said
in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai:

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת זוֹ וְאַחַת זוֹ צְרִיכָה בְּדִיקָה.
phrases.english: Both this and that require inspection.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the fire case and starts discussing the משנה's next case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird that was trampled or slammed against a wall must be checked after slaughter, even if it lived 24 hours.

steps.title: The משנה lists bird injuries that leave it kosher
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists injuries to a bird that do not make it a טרפה. רבי says the bird is kosher even if the crop was removed, and רבי יהודה says losing its down makes it unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: These injuries leave a bird kosher: a hole or crack in the windpipe, a weasel hitting its head in a place that doesn't make it טרפה, a hole in the crop (רבי: even if the crop was removed), intestines that came out without a hole, broken wings, broken legs, plucked wing feathers. רבי יהודה: if its down was removed, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives a list of bird injuries that do NOT make the bird a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the פרק listed injuries that make an animal or bird a טרפה. Now the משנה lists the opposite: injuries that look serious but leave the bird kosher. There are two disagreements: רבי is more lenient about the crop, and רבי יהודה is stricter about the down feathers.

keyTerms.meaning: The crop, a pouch in a bird's throat where food is held
The soft down feathers covering the bird's body

steps.whatToRemember: A hole in the crop leaves a bird kosher. רבי goes further and says that even if the whole crop is removed, the bird is still kosher.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are kosher among birds:
If the windpipe was perforated, or if it was cracked;
phrases.notes: 'Cracked' here means split along its length, not cut across.

phrases.english: if a weasel struck it on its head
in a place that does not make it a tereifa;
if the crop was perforated;
phrases.notes: The crop is a pouch in a bird's throat where food sits before it moves on to be digested.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: even if it was removed;
if its intestines came out but were not perforated;
if its wings were broken, if its legs were broken;
if its wing feathers were plucked.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם נִטְּלָה הַנּוֹצָה פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: If the down was removed, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of a bird that fell into fire and of trampled birds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These listed injuries leave a bird kosher. רבי permits even a removed crop, and רבי יהודה forbids a bird whose down was removed.

steps.title: Two sages ruled on a removed womb like רבי on the crop
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that רבי סימאי and רבי צדוק, staying in אונו on שבת, ruled about a טרפחת (womb) 'like רבי on the crop.'
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: רבי סימאי and רבי צדוק went to לוד to add a month to the year. They stayed in אונו for שבת, and there they ruled about a womb in line with רבי's view on the crop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a story connected to רבי's opinion in the משנה. Two sages gave a ruling about an animal's womb 'like רבי on the crop.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that רבי's view about the crop was used in a real ruling. But the wording is short and unclear. It does not say whether they permitted or forbade the womb case, and that opens the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a real story told as a source for הלכה
To make the year a leap year by adding a month

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
There was an incident with Rabbi Simai and Rabbi Tzadok
who went to make the year a leap year in Lod,
and they spent Shabbat in Ono,
and they ruled on a womb like Rabbi on the crop.
phrases.notes: The case is an animal whose womb was removed. The text doesn't say if they permitted or forbade it, and that's exactly what the next step asks.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי סִימַאי וְרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא story that refers to רבי's view on the crop from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי סימאי and רבי צדוק ruled on a removed womb in some connection to רבי's view on a removed crop.

steps.title: Was it two rulings or one comparison?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the story means. Either they forbade the womb case and separately permitted the crop case like רבי, or they permitted the womb case by comparing it to רבי's crop ruling while not actually holding like רבי about the crop.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Did they rule to forbid the womb case, and rule like רבי to permit the crop case? Or did they rule to permit the womb case by comparing it to רבי's crop ruling, while about the crop itself they don't hold like רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an איבעיא about how to read the short story. It offers two possible meanings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading one: two separate rulings. The womb case was forbidden, and the crop case was permitted like רבי. Reading two: one ruling. A removed womb is permitted, using רבי's logic that removing an organ like the crop does not make the animal טרפה, but they themselves do not hold like רבי about the crop.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them, an open question the גמרא tries to solve
Or perhaps, introducing the second option
They do not hold that view

steps.confusionAlert: In the second reading, the sages permit the womb case 'like רבי' but do NOT agree with רבי about the crop itself. They only borrowed his reasoning for a different organ.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Did they rule on the womb to forbid it,
and like Rabbi on the crop to permit it?
Or perhaps: they ruled on the womb to permit it
like Rabbi on the crop,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל כְּרַבִּי בְּזֶפֶק לָא סְבִירָא לְהוּ?
phrases.english: but they do not hold like Rabbi on the crop itself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand the unclear wording of the story in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did the sages forbid the womb case and permit the crop case like רבי, or did they permit the womb case by comparison to רבי while rejecting רבי on the crop?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the question with תיקו: it remains unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot decide between the two readings, so it leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No proof was found for either reading of the story. So we do not know for sure whether these sages permitted a removed womb, or whether they held like רבי on the crop.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the איבעיא of step 22 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It stays unknown which reading of the story is correct.

steps.title: The roof of the crop is treated like the gullet
steps.stepSummary: רבה (some say רבי יהושע בן לוי) teaches that the 'roof' of the crop has the same law as the ושט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said, and some say it was רבי יהושע בן לוי: The roof of the crop is judged like the gullet.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching limits the משנה's rule. Not every part of the crop is lenient: its upper part, the 'roof,' follows the law of the gullet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a hole in the crop does not make a bird טרפה. But a hole in the ושט (gullet) does make it טרפה. This teaching says the 'roof' of the crop counts as part of the gullet, so a hole there would make the bird טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'roof' of the crop, its upper part
Is judged like, has the same law as

steps.whyThisMatters: In practice, the משנה's leniency about a hole in the crop does not apply to the crop's upper section.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rabba said, and some say it was Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
The roof of the crop is judged like the gullet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's rule about a perforated crop and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The roof of the crop has the law of the ושט, not the lenient law of the crop.

steps.title: Where exactly is the roof of the crop?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which part of the crop counts as its 'roof.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition. It is setting up the next step, which explains where the 'roof' of the crop is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in step 24 is not useful unless we know where the 'roof' starts and ends. So the גמרא asks for its exact location.

phrases.english: Where is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the location of the 'roof' mentioned in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the crop is the 'roof' that is treated like the gullet?

steps.title: The roof is whatever stretches along with the gullet
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי defines the roof of the crop as any part that stretches together with the ושט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said: Any part that stretches along with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי בר אביי answers the question. The 'roof' is whatever part of the crop gets pulled along when the gullet is stretched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a practical test. If a part of the crop moves and stretches together with the ושט, it counts as gullet, and a hole there makes the bird טרפה. Other parts of the crop keep the משנה's lenient rule.
steps.whatToRemember: A hole in the crop is kosher, except in the 'roof': the part that stretches with the gullet. That part has the law of the ושט.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye said:
Any part that stretches with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The roof of the crop is any part of it that stretches together with the gullet.

steps.title: Intestines put back in the wrong order make the bird a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'its intestines came out.' רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק says the kosher ruling applies only if the intestines were not mixed up. If they were mixed up, the bird is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that if the bird's intestines came out, it is still kosher. רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said: this is only true if they were not turned around. But if they were turned around, it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה's case of intestines that came out. רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק adds a limit to the kosher ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the bird is kosher if the intestines came out but were not pierced. רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק says this only works if they go back in their proper order. If their order was switched, the bird becomes a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when... (a phrase that limits a ruling)
Turned around, mixed up the order
An animal or bird with a fatal defect, which is forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Its intestines came out,
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה's case of a bird whose intestines came out but were not pierced. The משנה says that bird is kosher.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הִיפֵּךְ בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: They only taught this where he did not turn them around,
but if he turned them around, it is a טרפה,
phrases.notes: He means the intestines were put back in the wrong order or position.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הִיפֵּךְ בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic from the משנה, moving on from the crop discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intestines that came out are kosher only if they were not reversed. If they were reversed, the bird is a טרפה.

steps.title: The פסוק proving each organ has a fixed place
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק brings 'הוא עשך ויכוננך' as his source. It teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא set fixed positions in a person, so if one of them is switched, the person cannot live.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'He made you and established you.' This teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא created fixed positions in a person, so that if one of them is turned around, he cannot live.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק backs up his ruling with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ויכוננך is read as כוננייות, which means set, fixed places. If an organ's place is switched, the body cannot survive. That is why mixed-up intestines make the bird a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed positions or bases for each organ
This teaches (shows what a פסוק comes to teach)

phrases.english: as it is written:
"He made you and established you,"
this teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created
fixed positions in a person,
phrases.notes: This is a play on the word וַיְכֹנְנֶךָ from the פסוק.

phrases.english: so that if one of them is turned around,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both just mean 'one.'

phrases.english: he cannot live.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the ruling in step 27
steps.raayaObject: That reversed intestines make the bird a טרפה
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 32:6, read as teaching that organs have fixed positions

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the Jewish people is a complete city
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי מאיר's reading of the same פסוק. The Jewish people is like a city with everything inside it. Its כהנים, prophets, officers and kings all come from within it, as the פסוק in זכריה says.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי מאיר would say: 'He made you and established you' means a city that has everything in it. From it come its כהנים, its prophets, its officers and its kings, as it says: 'From it the cornerstone, from it the peg...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different, אגדה-style explanation of the same פסוק it just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads ויכוננך as 'He built you complete.' The Jewish people does not need leaders from outside, because every kind of leader comes from within. This is not a halachic point. It is a side teaching on the same פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Cornerstone (here a picture of a leader)
Peg or stake (also a picture of a leader)
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir would say:
"He made you and established you" means
a city that has everything in it,
phrases.notes: He is describing the Jewish people as a city that has everything it needs inside it.

phrases.english: from it come its priests, from it come its prophets,
from it come its officers, from it come its kings,
as it is said:
"From it the cornerstone, from it the peg, and so on."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a non-halachic reading of the same פסוק used in step 28
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק teaches that the Jewish people is complete, and all its leaders come from within it.

steps.title: A story begins: a Roman sees a man whose intestines came out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a story. A Roman saw a man fall from a roof, and his belly burst open so his intestines came out. The Roman brought the man's son and slaughtered him in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain Roman saw a certain man fall from a roof to the ground. His belly burst open and his intestines came out. The Roman brought the man's son and slaughtered him in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about intestines coming out in a person, which connects back to step 27. This step only sets up the story, and the story keeps going in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story ties back to the topic of intestines coming out, now in a person instead of a bird. The point of the Roman's shocking act is not explained yet. The next lines finish the story.

phrases.english: A certain Roman
who saw a certain man
who fell from a roof to the ground,
his belly burst open
and his intestines came out,
he brought his son
and slaughtered him in front of him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of intestines coming out from step 27, now through a story about a person
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a story in which a man's intestines came out after a fall. The outcome continues in the next lines.
